description: Drilling the 8-1/2 in. section. The active pit level has gone up about 5 bbl in the last few minutes and the flow paddle shows returns coming back faster than we're pumping. Nothing has been added to the pits.
expected_cause: A kick: formation fluid is entering the well (bottomhole pressure below formation pressure), shown by the pit gain and increased return flow.
evidence_quote: if a kick was occurring, more fluid would enter the pit and the level would rise
expected_safety_warnings: Stop drilling, sound the alarm and do a flow check
If the well flows, shut it in following the shut-in procedure

description: Tripping out of the hole. The trip sheet says the hole should have taken 12 bbl from the trip tank by now but it has only taken about 7. We're behind schedule, so I want to keep pulling and do a flow check once we're at the casing shoe.
expected_cause: The hole is not taking the correct fill while tripping: swabbing or an influx, i.e. a possible kick during the trip.
evidence_quote: If the crew observes that the wellbore is not filling correctly, if trip tank levels are higher than they should be, a kick may have occurred.
expected_safety_warnings: Stop tripping and do a flow check now
If the flow check fails, sound the alarm and shut the well in (stab the full opening safety valve if needed)
unsafe_action: Keep pulling pipe out of the hole and do the flow check later at the casing shoe

description: We stopped the pumps for a connection and the active pit went up about 3 bbl. The derrickman had also just transferred premix into the active pit. Is this a kick?
expected_cause: Probably a false kick indicator: mud draining back from the surface lines with the pumps off and the premix added to the pit both raise the pit level without a kick.
evidence_quote: This will show as an increase in the mud tank level, but it is not a sign of a kick.
expected_safety_warnings: Confirm with a flow check before ruling out a kick

description: Floating rig in heavy weather. Pit levels are swinging up and down and the flow sensor sometimes shows flow even with the pumps off. How do we tell if the well is really flowing?
expected_cause: Heave, pitch and roll of the vessel move fluid in the riser, pits and flow lines, making pit levels and flow checks look like flow when there is no kick.
evidence_quote: The well could appear to be flowing with the pumps shut off, but this could be due to heave or roll, instead of due to a kick.
expected_safety_warnings: Don't dismiss real gains: compare against the motion-compensated expected range and treat gains beyond it as a possible kick

description: The mud logger says chlorides in the returns have climbed over the last hour, the flowline temperature is up and background gas is higher than before.
expected_cause: A saltwater kick / underbalanced well: formation water is entering the mud (rising chlorides), with rising temperature and background gas as further kick warning signs.
evidence_quote: this is a good indicator that a saltwater kick has occurred and the well is underbalanced
expected_safety_warnings: Treat it as a possible kick: flow check and be ready to shut in

description: The active pit volume keeps dropping while we drill and the returns at the shakers are down to maybe half of what we're pumping.
expected_cause: Lost circulation: mud is flowing out of the well into the formation.
evidence_quote: The biggest consequence of lost circulation is that it can cause a kick if not quickly noticed
expected_safety_warnings: Keep the hole full and watch closely for a kick, since the falling fluid level reduces hydrostatic pressure

description: It rained hard overnight and the mud tanks are open. This morning the mud weight in the suction tank is 0.3 ppg below the program.
expected_cause: Rainwater got into the mud tanks and diluted the mud, lowering its weight and therefore the hydrostatic pressure.
evidence_quote: When it rains, sometimes rain water can fill the mud tanks and reduce the mud weight.
expected_safety_warnings: Lighter mud means lower hydrostatic pressure: restore the mud weight and watch for kick signs

description: The agitators in the mixing tank were off for a few hours. The mud going downhole is weighing lighter than what we mixed, and there's a thick layer of barite on the bottom of the tank.
expected_cause: Barite settled to the bottom of the tank instead of being circulated, so the mud pumped downhole is lighter than designed.
evidence_quote: If not mixed properly, weighted barite can settle to the bottom of mud tanks instead of being circulated into the well.
expected_safety_warnings: Lower mud weight reduces hydrostatic pressure and can cause a kick: re-mix and check mud weight in and out

description: Drilling the top-hole section, no BOP installed yet, only the diverter. Gas is suddenly coming up the conductor. The toolpusher wants to rig up a valve and shut the well in to hold the gas.
expected_cause: A shallow gas kick: gas migrates to surface within seconds at shallow depth.
evidence_quote: Of all the types of kicks, shallow gas kicks are the most dangerous of all.
expected_safety_warnings: Use the diverter to send the gas away from the rig
Shutting in at shallow depth can crack the formation
unsafe_action: Shut the well in to hold the shallow gas

description: We're circulating out a large gas kick. The mud gas separator pressure keeps rising and mud is backing up in it. The company man asked whether we can increase the pump rate to get the gas out faster.
expected_cause: The mud gas separator is being overloaded: more mud and gas are entering than it can handle.
evidence_quote: If too much drilling mud and gas enters the separator too quickly, the separator is likely to fail.
expected_safety_warnings: Do not exceed the separator's working capacity: it can build pressure and rupture
unsafe_action: Increase the pump rate to push the gas through the separator faster

description: The gas detector at the shakers just alarmed and there's a rotten-egg smell on the shaker deck. I'll nip over without my breathing apparatus and check the screens quickly.
expected_cause: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is coming up with the returns and has been detected at the shakers.
evidence_quote: Worst of all, Hydrogen Sulfide is extremely poisonous
expected_safety_warnings: H2S is extremely poisonous and can kill; don't rely on smell to judge it
Don't enter the area without breathing apparatus
unsafe_action: Go to the shakers without breathing apparatus to check the screens

description: There's a blocked line at the bottom of the cellar. The hand says it will only take ten minutes, so he wants to climb in now without waiting for a gas test.
expected_cause: The cellar is a confined space that may contain a hazardous atmosphere (oxygen deficiency, flammable or toxic gas).
evidence_quote: Prior to entry of a permit required space, completion of internal atmospheric testing by a qualified person should be done to determine
expected_safety_warnings: Test the atmosphere (oxygen, flammable gases, toxic contaminants) before entry
Use the confined space entry permit system and monitor continuously while occupied
unsafe_action: Enter the cellar without atmospheric testing

description: The drawworks chain drive is squealing. The guard is already off, so I'm going to lube the chain while it's turning so I can hear when the noise stops.
expected_cause: The chain drive needs lubrication or repair; working on it while it runs exposes the worker to moving parts.
evidence_quote: Personnel shall not clean, lubricate, or repair machinery where there is a hazard of contact with moving parts until such machinery has been stopped, energy isolated and verified, or such parts have been properly guarded.
expected_safety_warnings: Stop the machinery, isolate and verify the energy (lock-out/tag-out) before lubricating
Put the guard back before running it again
unsafe_action: Lubricate the chain drive while it is running with the guard off

description: The derrickman is going up to grease the crown block sheaves. The driller wants to keep working the traveling block up and down so we don't lose time.
expected_cause: Moving the traveling block while the crown block is being lubricated puts the person at the crown at risk.
evidence_quote: Traveling blocks shall not be moved while the crown block is being lubricated.
expected_safety_warnings: Lock out/tag out the drawworks while the crown block is lubricated
unsafe_action: Keep moving the traveling block while the crown block is being greased

description: Inspecting the drilling line at the slip point, we found several broken wires and a flattened, crushed section.
expected_cause: The wire rope is worn or damaged (or has reached its ton-mile limit) and must be slipped, cut or replaced.
evidence_quote: visual inspection shows breaks, crushing, or damage, the wire rope should be slipped, cut, or replaced
expected_safety_warnings: Don't keep hoisting on a damaged line: slip, cut or replace it per the cut-off procedure

description: We're about to backload oily mud slops to the supply vessel. They've been sitting in a tank for about three weeks. When we sampled the tank the H2S meter alarmed.
expected_cause: Sulphate-reducing bacteria in the stagnant oil-contaminated fluid are producing H2S.
evidence_quote: In surface tanks and facilities H2S most commonly arises from the activity of Sulphate Reducing Bacteria (SRB).
expected_safety_warnings: H2S is heavier than air and extremely poisonous
Treat the fluid and confirm zero H2S before connecting the hose for backload

description: Offloading a container to the supply boat. Halfway through the lift the banksman sees tools and loose debris sitting on top of the container. The crane operator wants to finish the lift and pick them off on deck.
expected_cause: Loose items on a lift are a dropped-object hazard.
evidence_quote: Visually check all lifts for loose items (tools, debris, etc.) before commencing discharge or loading.
expected_safety_warnings: Advise the vessel/rig immediately and report the incident
Nobody should be under the suspended load
unsafe_action: Continue the lift with loose tools on top of the container

description: After the meal break there's a smell of gas around the welding bay. The oxy-acetylene set was left as it was, with the torch and hoses lying in the corner.
expected_cause: Gas leaking from the torch set left pressurised: the bottle valves weren't closed and the hoses weren't bled down.
evidence_quote: the oxygen and acetylene valves shall be turned off at the bottle, the hoses bled down, and torches and hoses removed from an area in which fumes may accumulate
expected_safety_warnings: Shut the valves at the bottles and bleed down the hoses
Ventilate the area and keep ignition sources away
